dial.summary: Six of eight indicators remain constructive on August 21: 2s10s steepened to +52bps (DGS10 4.71% minus DGS2 4.19%), DXY broke below 99 to 98.86 (lowest since late May after the US Treasury doubled its long-term buyback program), BTC funding rates compressed to +0.0025%/8h (near-zero, no overheating signal), ISM Manufacturing at 55.6% (highest since May 2022), Global M2 in sustained uptrend, Fed Balance Sheet flat at ~$6.76T; real yields eased to 2.35% from 2.44% but remain the lone structural headwind above the 2% threshold; BTC dominance at 56.2% — approaching the 55% Alt Rotation trigger but not yet sustained below it — with total crypto at ~$2.46T; dial holds BTC Accumulation with PCE (August 26) and Warsh's inaugural Jackson Hole keynote (August 28) as decisive catalysts.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) carried at ~$102.7T — July aggregate not yet published (~6-week reporting lag); US M2 confirmed at $23.16T for June 2026, +5.6% YoY (28th consecutive monthly increase, record high); no YoY contraction signal from any major central bank; 4-week trend up based on sustained US M2 expansion and continued global central bank balance sheet stability; status supportive (4-week uptrend confirmed; YoY contraction headwind condition not triggered).

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: July 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.6% (released August 3) remains the most recent reading — August 2026 data releases September 1, 2026; sub-indexes: New Orders 56.7%, Production 58.5%, Employment 52.8% (first factory hiring expansion in 18 months), Prices Paid 71.1%; July reading is the highest since May 2022; 4-week trend up: June 53.3% → July 55.6% = +2.3pp; status supportive (above 50 and rising; headwind thresholds of <48 falling or >62 not met).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 98.86 on August 21, 2026 (up 0.03% intraday; August 20 close ~98.76, the lowest since late May after the US Treasury doubled its long-term buyback program, breaking DXY below 99 for the first time since late May); 4-week trend down: DXY was ~101.2 around July 21 → 98.86 on August 21 = approximately -2.3%, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; status NEUTRAL (ICE DXY in the 97.5–100 neutral band; a sustained move below 97.5 would flip to supportive — PCE August 26 and Warsh Jackson Hole keynote August 28 are the key directional catalysts; Treasury buyback expansion adds structural downside pressure).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 at 2.35% as of August 19-20, 2026 — compressed from 2.44% on August 17 as nominal 10Y eased slightly from the August 17 peak; 4-week trend up: ~2.18% (July 21) → 2.35% (August 19) = +17bps, above the 5bps flat threshold; status headwind (above the 2% absolute threshold; soft July PCE August 26 and dovish Warsh keynote August 28 are the catalysts needed to compress real yields meaningfully below 2%; compression from 2.44% to 2.35% is a positive directional signal but the structural headwind persists).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: August 21, 2026: DGS10 rose to 4.71% (rebounding from 4.64% on August 20, erasing prior-day drop as the Treasury's larger buyback announcement pushed long yields higher); DGS2 at 4.19% (latest confirmed August 19; August 21 FRED release pending); spread = +52bps; 4-week trend up: ~+35bps (July 21) → +52bps (August 21) = +17bps steepening, above the 5bps flat threshold; status supportive (positive spread AND sustained 4-week steepening trend intact; a hawkish Warsh tone August 28 could flatten the curve; PCE August 26 is the next key input).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,759,955M ($6.760T) for week ending August 12, 2026 (H.4.1 released August 13); H.4.1 for week ending August 19 released August 20 at 4:30 PM ET — specific figure not yet confirmed but balance sheet held near $6.76T based on available data (FRED series extends to August 19, 2026); 4-week trend flat: $6,738,190M (July 29) → $6,759,955M (August 12) = +$21,765M (+0.32%), within the 0.5% flat threshold; status supportive (balance sheet holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau with no aggressive QT signal).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual futures funding rate at +0.0025%/8h on August 21, 2026 — near-zero and well below the +0.04%/8h overheating headwind threshold; compressed from +0.004%/8h on August 20 despite BTC holding ~$69,581 post-August 20 surge; 30-day trend down: ~+0.006%/8h in late June/early July → +0.0025% on August 21; very low positive funding indicates balanced long/short sentiment, not overleveraged bullishness — supportive for continued BTC accumulation; CoinGlass egress blocked, direct verification advised.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$308B (August 13 data; USDT ~59% + USDC ~23% of supply) vs. total crypto market cap ~$2.46T on August 21 (BTC at ~$69,581 with BTC dominance at 56.2%, implying BTC market cap ~$1.39T); stablecoin dominance ~12.5% ($308B / $2,460B), down from 12.6% on August 20 and from 14.3% in mid-July; 30-day trend down: ~14.3% (mid-July) → 12.5% (August 21) = -1.8pp compression as capital rotated from stablecoins into risk assets; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — dominance rising while TOTAL rises — is the opposite of current dynamics).

upcoming.title: Consumer Confidence (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index for August 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — released the day before the PCE/GDP cluster; incorporates July NFP shock (−23K), hot core CPI (3.1%), FOMC Minutes (August 19), Flash PMI (August 21), and the broad crypto rally (BTC +8% to ~$69,581 on August 20; DXY fell below 99 on August 21); a sharp deterioration in confidence would raise Q3 recession risk and bolster the case for September rate cuts.

upcoming.title: PCE Price Index (July 2026)
upcoming.note: BEA Personal Income and Outlays at 8:30 AM ET — July PCE Price Index (Fed's preferred inflation gauge), Personal Income, and Personal Spending; arrives one day before Jackson Hole opens; hot core CPI (3.1% YoY, August 12) implies core PCE potentially 2.7–2.8% YoY; a reading above 2.8% strongly supports a September hike; a soft print (<2.5%) preserves the rate-cut path, reinforces BTC Accumulation, and could push DXY below 97.5 from current 98.86 — the single most important data print ahead of Jackson Hole.

upcoming.title: GDP 2nd Estimate (Q2 2026)
upcoming.note: BEA releases the second estimate of Q2 2026 GDP at 8:30 AM ET alongside July PCE, one day before Jackson Hole opens; July NFP shock (−23K) and hot core CPI (3.1%) have raised Q3 recession concerns; significant downward revisions alongside soft labor and hot inflation would reinforce the stagflation narrative and set the tone for Warsh's keynote the following morning.

upcoming.title: Jackson Hole Economic Symposium Opens (August 27–29)
upcoming.note: Kansas City Fed annual Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium begins at Jackson Lake Lodge, Wyoming — runs August 27–29; theme: 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy'; by the time proceedings open, markets will have processed PCE (August 26), GDP Q2 2nd estimate (August 26), Consumer Confidence (August 25), and Flash PMI (August 21); Warsh delivers his inaugural Jackson Hole keynote Friday morning August 28; FOMC September 15–16 is the next binding commitment.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 22, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending August 22, 2026 — released the opening morning of Jackson Hole; a sustained rise in claims arriving as Jackson Hole opens would immediately shape the tone for Fed Chair Warsh's inaugural keynote the next morning (August 28).

upcoming.title: Fed Chair Warsh Inaugural Jackson Hole Keynote
upcoming.note: Kevin Warsh delivers his inaugural Jackson Hole address Friday morning August 28 — the single most important macro event of this cycle for the crypto risk framework; by August 28 all macro inputs will be in hand (PCE August 26, GDP 2nd estimate August 26, Consumer Confidence August 25, Flash PMI August 21); a hawkish tone signaling September hike despite soft growth would sharply pressure risk assets; a neutral or dovish tone alongside soft PCE data would be the macro green light to extend the BTC rally (~$69,581) and could push DXY below 97.5; September 15–16 FOMC is the next binding commitment.

upcoming.title: Chicago PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Chicago Business Barometer for August 2026 at 9:45 AM ET — released on the same morning as Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote; additional regional manufacturing cross-check against July ISM surge (55.6%) and Flash PMI (August 21); a reading above 50 would add a constructive macro backdrop to any risk-positive tone from Warsh's address.
